To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Mo(IV)-bis-dithiolene model system catalyzes the N-oxide degradation reaction by the oxygen atom transfer pathway.

the N-oxide oxygen atom transfer reaction is a concerted process involving a square-pyramidal to octahedral geometry change of Mo(IV) and the reaction pathway is dependent on the tautomeric form of the nitroethenedaimine substrate.
the oxygen atom transfer reaction from the imine and enamine tautomers of nitroethenamine are kinetically favorable, while the reaction from the nitronate form is thermodynamically favorable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanistic aspects of the N- oxide reduction process in the presence of the Mo(IV)/S2O42-/H+ system, using nitroethenediame as a model compound for the H2-receptor antagonist.
the elucidation of the oxygen atom transfer mechanism in nitronic acid based drugs using the model system, [Mo(OMet)(mdt) 2](-) complex.

the elucidation of the mechanism for the oxygen transfer from the nitroethenediomine based drugs to the model system, [Mo(OM)(mdt) (2)] (-), which is the key step in the metabolic degradation of the H2 receptor antagonists.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oxygen atom transfer reaction from the imine form is the most favorable pathway in the presence of Mo(IV) dithiolene catalyst.
the oxygen atom transfer occurs from the nitronic form of nitroethene diamine in the active center of the N-oxides reductase enzyme.
the oxygen atom transfer reaction from the enamine and nitronic acid tautomers is more energetically favorable than the imine tautomers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Mo(IV)-bis-dithiolene model system can be used to explain the mechanism of degradation of nitro group in nitroethenamine based H2-receptors antagonists.
, the oxygen transfer reaction is thermodynamically favored for the nitronic acid and enamine tautomers, whereas the reaction is endothermic for the imine tautomers.
the oxygen atom transfer reaction from the imine form of nitroethene diamine is thermodynamically favorable, but kinetically disfavored.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Mo(IV)-bis-dithiolene model system is able to catalyze the degradation of nitric oxide based drugs by the oxygen atom transfer mechanism.
the oxygen atom transfer is the most feasible reaction pathway for the degradation of nitronated drugs by the N-oxidereductase enzyme.
, the Mo(IV)-bis-dithiolene complexes can be considered as a model system to understand the oxygen transfer reactions in the active site and also to develop new drugs for colon cancer.
